note: Literature confirms RNU2-2 variants cluster in conserved functional domains with recurrent de novo and biallelic changes producing a highly congruent, severe DEE.

evidence.text: Recurrent pathogenic RNU2-2 variants cause a distinctive severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by severe to profound impairment, status epilepticus, and sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: We identified recurrent pathogenic RNU2-2 variants in 4 of 672 (0.6%) patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) of unknown cause. An additional patient was subsequently included... Pathogenic variants in RNU2-2 cause a distinctive severe DEE.

numbers.metric: prevalence in DEEs of unknown cause

evidence.text: Variants in RNU2-2 cluster in conserved 5' functional domains and recurrent variants manifest as a highly concordant, severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

source.title: Phenotypic and transcriptomic characterization of biallelic RNU2‐2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: We identified 14 individuals from nine families with 12 ultra-rare biallelic RNU2-2 variants clustering in the conserved 5' domains... All individuals presented with a highly concordant, severe DEE, characterized by severe to profound intellectual disability, inability to walk or communicate, hyperkinesia, and refractory seizures.

numbers.metric: individuals with conserved 5' domain clustering variants
